ops.title: Two live launcher builds sharing a Label ping-pong forever — the lock serializes but does not order
ops.description:
Found 2026-08-01 by the P4.2a2 refuter, testing an orchestrator claim and falsifying part of it.

The claim under test: the phase-4 stable-program placement moves the write under Ensure's start
lock, and that lock subsumes the three guards the donor `service.StableProgram` had — a
digest/size/mtime sidecar, a newer-or-repair replace predicate, and a lockless stat fast path
(CHANGELOG.md:348-353, donor history — note these were never in daemonkit's own base).

Verdict: the sidecar and the *repair* half ARE subsumed — a full re-read of the target replaces
both. The lockless fast path is traded for a full binary read per Ensure. **The *newer* half is not
subsumed: the lock serializes but does not order.** Two concurrently-live launcher builds sharing a
Label ping-pong forever — A places A and evicts B, B places B and evicts A.

Inherent to `decide`'s "any mismatch is an upgrade", and it predates staging rather than being
introduced by the cut. Plausible trigger: a long-lived supervisor and a CLI on different builds,
both running Ensure against one Label.

Fixing it needs a version-ordering decision daemonkit has not taken — a content digest has no order.
The `version` package classifies and compares release and development builds and may be the seam.
That is its own design question, not a v0.21.0 blocker.

A separate donor guard WAS genuinely dropped and is not subsumed by anything: "a canonical return
that never follows a symlink at the final component". Its absence let a planted symlink at the
program path survive every convergence. That one is already fixed in the lane.

ops.text: Two concurrently-live launcher builds sharing one Label converge instead of alternately evicting each other
The ordering rule is stated wherever decide() treats a build mismatch as an upgrade
